view.name: Image Generator
view.description: Creates a new design from a brief and returns it as a new asset. The brief (design goal, platform, offer and other details) is settled with the user beforehand by the input collector; this agent writes the copy, sets the type and renders. For designs with overlaid text it outputs a layout specification, so that text is stored as editable blocks. Also creates further variations of an existing design, and redoes a design from its saved brief; both return new assets and leave the original unchanged.

skills.summary: Create a new design from a description.
examples: Create a poster for a jazz night with a deep blue palette.
Generate a product banner for a coffee brand, 1200 by 628 pixels.
Design a square social post announcing a summer sale.
Create a minimalist logo concept for a bakery called Crumb.

skills.summary: Create a new design in the style of a reference asset.
examples: Create a new flyer in the style of a2 v1 for a different event.
Generate a companion banner that matches the look of a1 v3.

skills.summary: Create a design for a purpose outside the standard catalog of design goals.
examples: Design a menu card for a cafe.
Create a wedding invitation with a floral border.
Make a certificate of completion for a coding course.

skills.summary: Redo a design from its saved brief, for a fresh take on the same request.
examples: Regenerate a1 v1 from the same brief.
Try the poster a2 again from scratch, same text and goal.
Redo a1 with the new product photo the user attached.

skills.summary: Create further variations of an existing design, keeping its brief and text but changing the composition. Each variation is a new asset.
examples: Create three more variations of a1 v2.
Give the user another version of a3 v1 with a different layout.
Make two alternatives of a2 v1 in the same style.

not_for: Judging or advising on a design.

required_inputs.name: brief
required_inputs.meaning: What the design should show and be for.

required_inputs.name: size
required_inputs.meaning: Dimensions or aspect ratio.

required_inputs.name: source_asset
required_inputs.meaning: The design to vary or redo.
required_inputs.applies_when: The task asks for variations or a redo of an existing design.

required_inputs.name: logo
required_inputs.meaning: The logo to place on the design.
required_inputs.default: the brand kit logo if there is one, otherwise none

produces.detail: A new asset at version 1, with its layout specification where text is overlaid.

view.name: Image Editor
view.description: Changes an existing design and returns it as a new version. Handles changes to named elements, text blocks, regions, the background and the image as a whole, including several changes to the same target in one task. Works on flat images and on designs that already have layers. Also resizes a design for other platforms, raises its resolution, restores an earlier version and exports it in another file format.

skills.summary: Move, resize, rotate, flip, reorder or align an element.
examples: Move the logo in a1 v2 to the top right corner.
Enlarge the product photo in a3 v1 by about a third.
Rotate the badge in a2 v4 so it sits level.
Bring the price tag in a5 v1 in front of the ribbon.
Centre the CTA button horizontally in a1 v3.

skills.summary: Change the wording or typography of a text block.
examples: Enlarge the headline in a1 v1.
Change the headline in a2 v2 to read "Summer Sale Ends Sunday".
Set the body text in a4 v1 in a heavier weight and dark grey.
Make the text in a1 v1 bigger without it occupying more area.
Correct the spelling of "Recieve" in the tagline of a3 v2.

skills.summary: Change an element's colour, fill, border, corner radius, opacity or shadow.
examples: Make the CTA button in a1 v1 orange.
Round the corners of the photo frame in a2 v1 to 24 pixels.
Add a soft drop shadow under the product in a3 v3.
Make the banner strip in a4 v2 half transparent.

skills.summary: Remove, add or replace an object or the background.
examples: Remove the lamp from the left side of a2 v1.
Change the background of a1 v1 to navy blue.
Replace the sky in a5 v2 with a clear sunset sky.
Add a small potted plant on the desk in a3 v1.

skills.summary: Adjust colour and tone of the whole image or a region.
examples: Make a1 v2 warmer and slightly brighter.
Increase the contrast of the product area in a4 v1.
Convert a2 v3 to black and white.
Increase the brightness of a1 v2 by 20.

skills.summary: Crop, resize, extend or reflow a design for another format.
examples: Produce a square version of a3 v2 for Instagram.
Crop a1 v1 to remove the empty space on the right.
Extend a2 v1 to a 16:9 banner, continuing the background.
Make an Instagram story version and a LinkedIn post version of a1 v2.

skills.summary: Raise the resolution or sharpness of a design.
examples: Upscale a1 v2 for print.
Increase the resolution of a3 v1 to 4K.
Sharpen the blurry product photo in a2 v1.

skills.summary: Bring back an earlier version of a design as its newest version.
examples: Undo the last change to a1, bringing back v2.
Go back to the first version of a3.

skills.summary: Return a design in another file format.
examples: Give the user a1 v3 as a transparent PNG.
Export a2 v1 as a JPG.

not_for: Creating a new design when no existing design is given.
Judging or scoring the quality of a design.
Advising what should be changed, or offering options for a change.
Extracting an element as a layer when the layer itself is the result wanted.
Finding and repairing generation artifacts when no specific change is requested.
Providing information about a design without changing it.
Changes the user wants to make by hand in a tool.
Creating further variations or alternative versions of a design.
Repairing malformed hands or faces, garbled lettering or other AI generation artifacts.

required_inputs.name: target_asset
required_inputs.meaning: The design version to change.

required_inputs.name: target
required_inputs.meaning: The element, text block, region or whole image the change applies to.

required_inputs.name: change
required_inputs.meaning: What is to be different about the target.

required_inputs.name: new_value
required_inputs.meaning: The value to change to, when the change replaces one value with another: a colour, wording, a font, a position.
required_inputs.applies_when: The change replaces a value and the task gives none.
required_inputs.on_missing: Ask the user, offering "suggest some" and "you choose".

required_inputs.name: amount
required_inputs.meaning: How much, for relative changes such as bigger, warmer or more rounded.
required_inputs.default: agent may choose; the chosen amount is stated in the result

required_inputs.name: preserve
required_inputs.meaning: Anything that must stay unchanged or limits the change.
required_inputs.default: everything outside the target stays as it is

produces.detail: A new version of the target asset, a list of the changes made, and any values the agent chose itself.

typical_assistance_needs: An element or text block separated as a layer.
Options for a value the user delegated.

view.name: ChitChat Handler
view.description: Holds a brief social exchange: greetings, thanks, pleasantries.

examples: Respond to the user's greeting.
Acknowledge the user's thanks.
Reply to a casual remark that asks for nothing.

not_for: Any request for information about a design or the system.
Any task that creates, changes or assesses a design.
